constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of fresh alfalfa may increase the risk of digestive disturbances and produce excessive dietary calcium.
constraints.recommendation: Reduce the amount of fresh alfalfa and replace part of it with grass hay or another roughage source.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion of mature fresh alfalfa may oversupply calcium and reduce dietary balance.
constraints.recommendation: Replace part of the alfalfa with grass forage to maintain a balanced forage composition.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of alfalfa hay can provide excessive calcium and protein beyond the animal's requirement.
constraints.recommendation: Use grass hay for part of the forage if calcium or crude protein exceeds the target.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion may lead to excess calcium and unnecessary protein intake.
constraints.recommendation: Replace part of the alfalfa hay with a lower-calcium forage.

constraints.warningMessage: Feeding excessive alfalfa hay may increase dietary calcium beyond the desired level.
constraints.recommendation: Balance the ration with grass hay to improve the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio.

constraints.warningMessage: Large quantities of barley grain increase the risk of starch overload, hindgut acidosis and colic.
constraints.recommendation: Reduce barley and replace part of the energy with fiber or fat sources.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive barley straw reduces digestibility and may increase the risk of impaction colic.
constraints.recommendation: Replace part of the straw with higher-quality forage.

constraints.warningMessage: Very high levels of beet pulp may reduce dietary balance and should be introduced gradually.
constraints.recommendation: Limit beet pulp and diversify fiber sources within the ration.

constraints.warningMessage: Large quantities of fresh berseem may increase the risk of digestive upset due to its high moisture content.
constraints.recommendation: Offer with dry forage such as hay or straw to improve fiber intake.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion may oversupply calcium and protein depending on the animal's requirements.
constraints.recommendation: Mix with grass hay to maintain a balanced forage composition.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of fresh corn forage may dilute dietary dry matter intake and increase the risk of digestive disturbances.
constraints.recommendation: Combine with dry forage such as hay to maintain adequate fiber and dry matter intake.

constraints.warningMessage: High levels of corn grain increase starch intake and may cause hindgut acidosis, colic and laminitis.
constraints.recommendation: Reduce corn grain and replace part of the energy with oats, beet pulp or vegetable oil.

constraints.warningMessage: Poor-quality corn silage or excessive inclusion may increase the risk of digestive disorders and spoilage-related problems.
constraints.recommendation: Use only high-quality silage and balance the ration with dry forage.

constraints.warningMessage: Corn stover is poorly digestible and excessive amounts may increase the risk of impaction colic.
constraints.recommendation: Replace part of the corn stover with higher-quality forage.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive cottonseed may increase gossypol intake and reduce diet safety.
constraints.recommendation: Limit cottonseed and diversify protein sources with soybean meal or linseed meal.

constraints.warningMessage: Animal fat is generally not recommended as a primary fat source for horses.
constraints.recommendation: Use vegetable oil instead of animal fat whenever possible.

constraints.warningMessage: Rapid introduction or excessive vegetable oil may reduce fiber digestion and feed intake.
constraints.recommendation: Increase oil gradually and keep adequate forage in the diet.

constraints.warningMessage: Fish meal is highly concentrated and excessive use may reduce palatability and oversupply minerals.
constraints.recommendation: Reserve fish meal for specialized formulations and keep inclusion low.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion of horse beans may reduce digestibility and increase digestive disturbances.
constraints.recommendation: Mix horse beans with other protein ingredients instead of using them alone.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive linseed meal may increase dietary fat and reduce ration balance.
constraints.recommendation: Use together with other protein sources instead of as the sole protein ingredient.

constraints.warningMessage: High levels of millet forage may reduce overall nutrient density of the ration.
constraints.recommendation: Combine millet with higher-quality forage.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive molasses increases sugar intake and may contribute to obesity, insulin dysregulation and laminitis.
constraints.recommendation: Limit molasses and replace excess energy with fiber or oil.

constraints.warningMessage: Although safer than corn, excessive oats still increase starch intake.
constraints.recommendation: Split grain between meals and maintain adequate forage intake.

constraints.warningMessage: High levels of oat straw may reduce digestibility and increase the risk of impaction colic.
constraints.recommendation: Use oat straw only as part of the forage source, not as the primary forage.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion of peanut meal may reduce amino acid balance and increase the risk of aflatoxin exposure if feed quality is poor.
constraints.recommendation: Use peanut meal with other protein sources and ensure the ingredient is free from mold contamination.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of rice bran may create an inverted calcium-to-phosphorus ratio and increase phosphorus intake.
constraints.recommendation: Balance rice bran with adequate calcium supplementation such as limestone or alfalfa.

constraints.warningMessage: High levels of rice grain increase starch intake and may predispose horses to hindgut acidosis and digestive upset.
constraints.recommendation: Limit rice grain and combine it with adequate forage and slowly fermentable energy sources.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive sorghum grain may reduce starch digestibility and increase digestive disturbances.
constraints.recommendation: Mix sorghum with other grains and avoid making it the sole concentrate source.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of soybean meal may oversupply crude protein beyond the horse's requirement.
constraints.recommendation: Use soybean meal only to meet protein requirements and combine it with energy ingredients.

constraints.warningMessage: High inclusion of sunflower meal increases dietary fiber and may reduce energy density.
constraints.recommendation: Balance sunflower meal with higher-energy ingredients when required.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of wheat bran provide excessive phosphorus and may disrupt the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio.
constraints.recommendation: Always balance wheat bran with calcium-rich ingredients.

constraints.warningMessage: High wheat grain intake may increase the risk of starch overload, colic and hindgut acidosis.
constraints.recommendation: Feed wheat grain in limited amounts and provide sufficient forage.

constraints.warningMessage: High levels of wheat straw reduce digestibility and may increase the risk of impaction colic.
constraints.recommendation: Use wheat straw only as a partial forage source and combine it with good-quality hay.

constraints.warningMessage: Excessive bone meal may oversupply calcium and phosphorus and disturb mineral balance.
constraints.recommendation: Use bone meal only to correct phosphorus or calcium deficiencies identified by the formulation engine.

constraints.warningMessage: Excess calcium carbonate may produce an excessively high calcium-to-phosphorus ratio.
constraints.recommendation: Only supplement calcium carbonate when dietary calcium is below the requirement.

constraints.warningMessage: Excess dicalcium phosphate may oversupply both calcium and phosphorus.
constraints.recommendation: Use only the quantity required to meet mineral requirements.

constraints.warningMessage: Excess limestone may produce an excessively high calcium intake and an imbalanced calcium-to-phosphorus ratio.
constraints.recommendation: Supplement limestone only when calcium is deficient.

constraints.warningMessage: Large amounts of oyster shell may provide unnecessary calcium and reduce mineral balance.
constraints.recommendation: Use oyster shell only when additional calcium is required.

constraints.warningMessage: Excess sodium phosphate may oversupply phosphorus and disturb the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio.
constraints.recommendation: Supplement sodium phosphate only when phosphorus deficiency exists.
